correctness.rationale: A normalized invariant law follows from exponentially distributed reset ages and exact Gaussian–Laplace convolution. A positive Gaussian-variance mixture shows g/phi strictly increases and crosses one uniquely beyond sigma, giving the sharp curvature sign. The Gaussian variation-diminishing property applied to the three-sign-change derivative of a symmetric Laplace pair proves global modality, including the cubic central derivative zero at criticality. Exact Green-kernel derivatives give the pitchfork coefficient; Gaussian moment expansions and elementary convolution bounds prove both endpoint asymptotics. Standalone checker independently passed 213 finite evaluations; only analytic steps certify universal statements.

value.rationale: Resetting to two spatial Gaussian populations is a natural stochastic-transport model. The stationary law can suppress already-present source bimodality and has one sharp, explicitly characterizable finite-rate threshold, a quartic critical flatness and precise peak splitting. Its rare-reset sqrt-log separation requirement quantifies a meaningful, otherwise hidden competition between reset heterogeneity and Brownian excursions. This is a structured phase diagram rather than an arbitrary constant or routine numerical evaluation.
